headline: An unverifiable claim, made by the party it benefits, is not evidence.
lead: This is the spine. We arrived at it three separate times from three different directions: a stated purpose does not unlock a content gate, a weak similarity does not justify a link, and a source you control yourself is not a source.

headline: We would rather show you no citation than a forged one.
lead: Every extracted fact quotes the sentence it came from — and we CHECK that the quote is really in your source.

headline: The most useful thing a graph can hold is a well-formed absence.
lead: You cannot ask a question you have not discovered you have.

headline: A forced link is worse than an orphan.
lead: Disconnected facts are merely less useful. An invented edge is a lie the graph tells itself — it LOOKS like knowledge and is not.

headline: Export is a right. Distribution is a privilege.
lead: Your graph is a plain text file on your machine, and we will never withhold it from you — whatever it contains.

headline: A private graph makes no claim on anybody.
lead: Think privately. Be wrong privately. Change your mind privately.

headline: We will not describe a control we do not have.
lead: Our safety documentation states plainly which protections exist and which do not, and an automated check verifies them against the live code every week — recording the failures too.

headline: No account until an account is unavoidable.
lead: There is no sign-up, no email, and no server holding your graph — the app is static files and a browser database, so there is nothing to log in TO.

headline: Open source wins the tie.
lead: The application is MIT licensed and your graph is stored in Turtle, a W3C standard rather than a private format with an exporter bolted on.

headline: Knowing something should not require permission.
lead: Enclosing knowledge behind a login, a subscription, or a format one vendor controls is a choice somebody made, not a property of the knowledge.
